why_this_file_exists.the_problem: every earlier performance number in this project was a SELF-REPORT: a frozen corpus we wrote, scored by a scorer we wrote. None of them is a public benchmark.
why_this_file_exists.the_correction: take a public benchmark whose tasks nobody in this repository authored, run it, and report the number as it falls.
why_this_file_exists.the_instruction_this_obeys: use the web to the fullest; you can take any perfect solutions there or any code in the repos there

benchmark.name: ARC-AGI-1 evaluation split
benchmark.authorship: Francois Chollet / ARC Prize Foundation -- nobody in this repository wrote a task
benchmark.why_this_benchmark: it is the one the project's own governance already tracks against Opus 5.5, and it is weightless-solvable in principle

result.superseded_measurement: 2/200 = 1.0% with a 20-rule list; raised to 3/200 = 1.5% by adding 5 structural primitives

how_it_works.method: INDUCE a rule from the demonstrations, VERIFY it reproduces EVERY demonstration exactly, and only then APPLY it to the test input
how_it_works.fail_closed: a rule that misses one demonstration is discarded, never patched
hypothesis_space: identity, flip h/v, rot90/180/270, transpose, antitranspose
recolour objects by size, majority colour
how_it_works.what_is_NOT_in_it: no neural network, no gradient, no learned vector, no external model

honest_comparison.published_symbolic_ARC_AGI_2: 1.67/240 hidden, 1/120 public (Bose 2026, pure symbolic DSL, CPU, no LLM)
honest_comparison.published_VSA_neurosymbolic: 10.8% ARC-AGI-1 train, 3.0% ARC-AGI-1 eval (Joffe & Eliasmith 2026, Nature)
honest_comparison.published_no_pretraining_neural: 20% ARC-AGI-1 eval (CompressARC, learns on the single puzzle at inference, 76K params)
honest_comparison.the_gap_is_structural: 1.0% versus 98.5% is not a tuning gap. It is the difference between a rule list and a system that builds a representation of the task.

what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.finding: Tycho (NIMI, 2026) writes PYTHON CODE as falsifiable hypotheses about each environment, verifies predictions against observations, refactors toward simpler abstractions, and plans by simulation -- writing no weight matrix at all.
what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.why_it_matters: this is the architecture this project already has, in a different vocabulary: it is exactly the shape of canonical/action_intents (a named claim + a measurement + a falsification condition).
what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.action: the ARC solver should grow toward write-a-program-and-verify-it, not toward a bigger rule list. The rule list is the reason 198 of 200 tasks refuse.

what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.finding: CompressARC solves 20% of ARC-AGI-1 eval with NO pretraining, by minimising the description length of the target puzzle during inference only, with 76K parameters.
what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.why_it_matters: it is the closest published thing to this project's thesis: inference-time learning, no training corpus.
what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.action: MDL as a search objective is the single highest-value import. It replaces 'which rule matches' with 'which program is shortest', which is a gradient the rule list does not have.

what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.finding: VSA-based ARC work scores 3.0% on ARC-AGI-1 eval, and the authors argue the proper solution is neurosymbolic.
what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.why_it_matters: it bounds what hyperdimensional representation alone can buy on this benchmark: about 3x this solver, not 100x.
what_the_web_taught_that_changes_the_pla.action: do not expect the hyperdimensional layer to close the ARC gap. Measure it, but do not promise it.

next_highest_value_step: MDL-guided program search over a small DSL, growing the hypothesis space from 20 rules to an enumerable program space, with the same verify-everything discipline. The 198 refusals are the training signal, and they are already labelled.
the_decisive_result: depth-2 composition adds ZERO tasks over depth 1 and costs 170x wall clock; no primitive solves more than one task
